data_fields.name: staff_timer_base_units
data_fields.donor_constant: 5000 (10000 for blinking and obstruction) divided by enchant

data_fields.name: staff_timer_tick_per_turn
data_fields.donor_constant: 10 per call, times the wisdom multiplier

data_fields.name: staff_rearm_high_fraction
data_fields.donor_constant: D x 5 / 3, then drain above it

data_fields.name: staff_max_charges
data_fields.donor_constant: enchant1 = generated charges; row range {2,4,1} plus 15% bonus, 10% chain

data_fields.name: reaping_recharge_share
data_fields.donor_constant: rand(0, min(damage, victim HP) x reaping)

data_fields.name: full_regen_turns
data_fields.donor_constant: 300 at regen bonus 0, x 0.75 per bonus point, +2 turn floor

data_fields.name: charm_recharge_base_and_min
data_fields.donor_constant: duration + rechargeDelayDuration x rechargeDelayBase^enchant, minimum rechargeDelayMinTurns

best_idea: Magic as charged items, not a character pool: each staff keeps a charge count and one random re-arm timer (about D/3 to 5D/3 per charge, D from the enchant), and a weapon property (reaping) refills or drains that timer, so melee and staff use trade on one clock.
decision_why: Take the charge-timer shape and the enchant curves as item and table data for our specials (row 13). Keep the donor's fizzle-costs-a-turn rule. Do not copy the entrancement overwrite (Items.c 4594); use the max rule the discord branch uses (Items.c 4641). Use floats on the server, not the donor's fixed-point tables.
acceptance: Server test: a staff with 3 max charges, fully emptied, returns its first charge after 56 to 278 turns (mean about 167); a 40-damage hit on a 100-HP foe with reaping +1 shifts the timer by a random 0 to 40 units; an empty identified staff refuses the zap without ending the turn.
